label: Figure 8
title: SBIR/STTR from Phase I to Phase III, with the branches around it
caption: SBIR and STTR run in three phases. Phase I tests feasibility, with a base guideline of $150,000; Phase II continues the work, with a base guideline of $1,000,000; Phase III is work that derives from, extends or completes the earlier work and is paid from other funds, with no limit on number, duration, type or dollar value [5](#cite:5). As of April 2026 agencies may go to $323,090 and $2,153,927 without seeking SBA approval [11](#cite:11). Around that line sit the branches. Direct to Phase II skips Phase I on a written determination of demonstrated feasibility and now runs until September 30, 2031 at NIH, DoD, Education, DOE and NASA [5](#cite:5) [1](#cite:1). Fast-Track, at NSF, joins a $400,000 Phase I component to a Phase II of up to $1,155,000 in one award [35](#cite:35). One sequential Phase II may follow the first [5](#cite:5). The Strategic Breakthrough award is not more than $30,000,000 over not more than 48 months and needs at least one prior Phase II award and not less than 100 percent matching funds [1](#cite:1). After Phase II, agency transition programs add money or help: TACFI and STRATFI [236](#cite:236), Army CATALYST [239](#cite:239), the Navy's STP [235](#cite:235), ART [55](#cite:55), APFIT [108](#cite:108) [109](#cite:109), NIH's Commercialization Readiness Pilot [31](#cite:31) and NSF's Phase IIB supplement [35](#cite:35). An agency may award Phase III sole source under 15 U.S.C. 638(r)(4) [225](#cite:225).
how_to_read: Follow the heavy line left to right for the standard path: Phase I, Phase II, Phase III. The boxes above and below Phase I are other ways in, and both arrive at Phase II. The boxes after Phase II are what can follow it before or alongside Phase III; the list under the transition box names the agency programs. Open a box in the app to see its amounts, time limits and the text behind them. The figure shows what the rules allow, not what any agency will fund in a given year.

explain.text: Not a third award from the SBIR budget. It is any work that derives from, extends or completes Phase I or II work, funded from other sources, and the size limits for Phases I and II do not apply to it [5](#cite:5).
The posted directive still lists only NIH, DoD and Education and an expired date; Pub. L. 119-83 extended the authority to September 30, 2031 and added DOE, NASA and STTR [5](#cite:5) [1](#cite:1).

A new tier in the 2026 act for agencies whose required SBIR spending exceeds $100,000,000. Defense awards carry extra conditions, including a commitment from a senior acquisition official [1](#cite:1).
NIH also offers Fast-Track and counts those applications in its per-firm limit of nine a fiscal year [31](#cite:31) [29](#cite:29).

Each has its own eligibility and matching rule. APFIT is procurement funding that only a government organisation can request on a firm's behalf; the firm must be a small business, a nontraditional defense contractor, or one with no more than $400,000,000 in contracts in the prior year [109](#cite:109).

nodes.label: Small firm with a technology
nodes.detail: Not more than 500 employees with affiliates; ownership per 13 CFR 121.702.

nodes.label: Phase I
nodes.detail: Feasibility. Base guideline $150,000; normally not more than 6 months (SBIR) or 1 year (STTR). Up to $323,090 without SBA approval as of April 2026.

nodes.label: Phase II
nodes.detail: Continues the Phase I effort. Base guideline $1,000,000; normally not more than 2 years. Up to $2,153,927 without SBA approval as of April 2026.

nodes.label: Phase III
nodes.detail: Work that derives from, extends or completes earlier SBIR/STTR work, paid from non-SBIR/STTR funds. No limit on number, duration, type or dollar value; sole source under 15 U.S.C. 638(r)(4).

nodes.label: Direct to Phase II
nodes.detail: A Phase II without a prior Phase I, on a written determination of demonstrated feasibility. Until September 30, 2031; NIH, DoD and Education, with DOE and NASA and STTR added by Pub. L. 119-83.

nodes.label: Fast-Track
nodes.detail: One award with a Phase I component followed by a Phase II component. NSF 26-510: $400,000 over 6 to 12 months plus up to $1,155,000 over a further 18 to 24 months. Also available at NIH.

nodes.label: Sequential (second) Phase II
nodes.detail: One additional, sequential Phase II to continue the work of an initial Phase II, on the same terms.

nodes.label: Strategic Breakthrough award
nodes.detail: Not more than $30,000,000 over not more than 48 months; not less than 1 prior Phase II award; not less than 100 percent matching funds. Authority ends September 30, 2031.

nodes.label: Transition programs after Phase II
nodes.detail: Agency programs that add money or help between Phase II and Phase III.

nodes.label: TACFI (Air Force)
nodes.detail: $375,000 to $2 million, up to 24 months, 1:1 match.

nodes.label: STRATFI (Air Force)
nodes.detail: $3 million to $15 million of SBIR/STTR funds, up to 48 months, with matching funds.

nodes.label: Army SBIR CATALYST
nodes.detail: Base award $1 million; enhancement up to $7 million additional SBIR funds; match 2:1:1 (Army SBIR : Army customer : integrator).

nodes.label: Navy STP
nodes.detail: An 11-month assistance program for Navy Phase II awardees who have not elected TABA.

nodes.label: ART (DoW)
nodes.detail: 1:1 matching of a DoW agency or component's funding for Phase II projects; the sponsor signs a Technology Transition Agreement.

nodes.label: APFIT (DoW)
nodes.detail: Procurement funding only, $10 million to $50 million per project; only government organisations submit on behalf of companies.

nodes.label: NIH Commercialization Readiness Pilot
nodes.detail: $4,191,495 for a project timeline of up to 3 years.

edges.label: Phase I and Phase II in one award
Phase III may follow Phase I work
